conventions.origin: every module's footing sits at z = 0
conventions.glb: glTF 2.0 binary; metres, Y-up per the glTF specification
conventions.fbx: binary FBX; vertex values in CENTIMETRES with UnitScaleFactor 1, Z-up, X-forward -- both readings agree, so Import Uniform Scale stays 1.0. See forge/units.py.
conventions.materials: one material slot per mesh; a module with several materials exports one mesh per material, sharing an origin. Names are the MI_V2_* instances already in wonderland/v2/materials_v2.py.
conventions.uv: planar-world projection at 2 m per tile; NOT a lightmap unwrap

stone.use: the pale ashlar the reference's towers are cut from

stone_dark.use: shadowed masonry: undercrofts, arch soffits, buttress cores

roof.use: the rose cone roofs that give the skyline its colour

roof_alt.use: the second roof colour, so a district is not one hue

metal.use: railings, ties, hinges, the structural non-gold

gold.use: leaf gold: finials, filigree, the reference's loudest accent

gold_aged.use: gold that has been outside -- large ornament, so it is not all bright

glass.use: lit glazing; emissive in the V2 material

glass_cool.use: the cool glazing, for contrast against the amber

veg_anchor.use: an ivy/planting attachment surface, not a plant

water.use: a still water surface; a flat lid on a basin with real depth

water_lit.use: falling and lit water -- cascades, spouts, the emissive teal

paving.use: the walked surface: plaza slabs, landings, the top of a step

paving_warm.use: the second tint, so a laid surface has more than one stone in it

paving_shade.use: the dark inlay: a medallion's band, a runnel's floor, a joint

enamel.use: a clock dial: the pale face inside a gold case

lawn.use: the sward on a floating island: the ground a castle foot stands on

kerb.use: kerbs, gutters, tree surrounds -- the edge of the made surface
